name: Is a corner lot better for vacant-lot development?

mainEntity.name: Is a corner vacant lot better or worse for development than an interior lot in Los Angeles neighborhoods?
mainEntity.text: Is a corner vacant lot better or worse for development than an interior lot in Los Angeles neighborhoods?

acceptedAnswer.text: Corner lots can be excellent development sites because they often provide easier access, more frontage, and greater design flexibility than interior parcels. That can help with driveway placement, garage location, and architectural presence. However, corner lots can also be harder to shape efficiently because they may face setbacks on two sides, have more public exposure, and create privacy or noise issues for a residence. In some cases, corner conditions reduce the practical buildable area even when the parcel looks larger on paper. The right answer depends on whether the goal is a single luxury home, a duplex, or a small multifamily project. For a high-end custom build, a corner lot may offer a stronger street presentation. For maximum land efficiency, an interior lot may be simpler. A site study should compare both the visible curb appeal and the actual buildable envelope before deciding.
acceptedAnswer.description: A corner lot can offer stronger visibility, better access, and more design flexibility, but it can also bring more setback exposure, privacy challenges, and streetscape constraints. Whether it is better depends on the project type and zoning.
